purpose: check that code follows the agreed standards by automated tools and a short human pass, and keep standards honest by tracking exceptions
procedure: Run the formatter check, linter, type checker and secret scan on the change, and collect the results in one report.
Treat any new suppression comment as a finding that needs a stated reason and an owner.
Look at what tools cannot judge: naming that misleads, missing error handling and unclear structure.
Check that the tool configuration itself was not weakened in the same change.
Report findings with file, rule and the standard section, and separate blockers from suggestions.
Feed recurring human findings back as a new automated rule or a standard update.
acceptance_criteria: All tools ran on the change

validation.command: ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src   # example; use the language's tools
git diff origin/main -U0 | grep -nE 'noqa|type: ignore|eslint-disable|nosec' | head
validation.expect: each added suppression has a reason in the review

failure_modes.detection: Config changed in the same change
failure_modes.response: Review the config change on its own

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A change adds two suppression comments. One has a reason and a ticket; the other hides a real unused variable and is removed. The reviewer proposes a lint rule for the pattern seen in three recent reviews.
